review_type: Independent scientific review - pre-sign-off analysis and change request
scope: All 650 profiles. No assignment list exists in the repository, packets or prior sessions, and every profile is produced by one generator, so the generator's rules were reviewed across all profiles, with representative profiles checked against the running engine.

verdict_definitions.BLOCK: The profile's own rules or fixtures certify a scientifically false result - a wrong unit, scale or axis structure, or an impossible conversion - so approving it would freeze that error into the conformance suite.
verdict_definitions.CHANGES_REQUIRED: No false result is certified by this profile's own fixtures, but the systemic blockers leave the contract too imprecise to approve.

reviewer_status.statement: This analysis was produced by an AI assistant (Claude Opus 5) at the request of the repository owner. It is not a qualified, independent, domain-specific scientific sign-off and must not be recorded as one. PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires a named scientific reviewer who did not author the profile and a different named schema reviewer; git history attributes all profile source to one author, so both must come from outside that authorship.
reviewer_status.evidence_policy: No file was written under source/reviews/. Every profile carries at least one blocking change, and review evidence may only be created after blocking changes are incorporated.
reviewer_status.sha256_pinning: Sources are pinned in docs/scientific-remediation/sources/sources.lock.json. Read the pinned_as field before relying on a digest: a document pin covers the reviewed text, a citation-metadata pin covers only the Crossref record for the DOI, and licensed standards (ISO 80000-1, ISO 20776-1, SNOMED CT) cannot be pinned here at all. Where a decision rests on a paywalled or licensed text, the reviewer pins their own copy and records the terms.
reviewer_status.repository_changes: None. No file under spec/v0.1/ or source/ was modified.

digest_check.method: SHA-256 over the sorted-key compact JSON of the full profile definition, reproducing scripts/build_standard.py digest()

ensembl.gene vs hgnc.symbol namespaces, declared on both ports

Firing rate in nM vs uM - the profile's own conversion fixture

Species 'any' on the source vs NCBITaxon:9606 on the target

engine_verification.scientifically_correct: Decided by UBERON/OBI subsumption against a pinned snapshot

concept_identifier_decision.decision: Keep a Biosimulant-controlled term, re-minted in a version-independent namespace, and require a mapping to external ontology terms.

rejected_alternatives.replace with an external identifier only: No external ontology defines 'a Biosimulant port contract for X'; an external term alone cannot carry the profile's contract boundary, and forcing one would overstate equivalence.

concept_identifier_decision.required_mapping: semantic.ontology_terms[] with uri, ontology, version and relation; compared by term-equivalent or term-subsumes against a pinned snapshot

errata.title: The per-profile verdict split is withdrawn
errata.detail: 136 BLOCK / 514 CHANGES_REQUIRED implied a per-profile precision the evidence does not support, because nearly every defect originates in shared generator and comparison code. The single conclusion is that all 650 profiles are unsuitable for GA review until those foundations are fixed. The per-profile table below survives only as an index of which profiles show which symptom.

errata.title: S12 miscounted the security profiles
errata.detail: The 50 profiles requiring security.data_use and security.consent_scope are 25 clinical and 25 epidemiology, not 50 clinical.

errata.title: The blanket candidate-item decisions are withdrawn
errata.detail: Several were over-broad: uncertainty.censoring was marked required in 400 packets although its own reason limits it to time-to-event data; semantic.ontology_terms was marked required for all 650; artifact.sha256 required wherever an artifact representation is allowed. Item levels are now decided per profile or profile class (decision D10), with this table as input only.

errata.title: Four conclusions were stated too absolutely
errata.detail: Dense-to-sparse re-encoding is lossless only when implicit-entry meaning, ordering, shape and dtype are declared equal (D6). Celsius to kelvin is exact for absolute temperatures; a temperature difference converts with factor 1 and no offset (D1). Identifier mapping is not always lossy: a pinned, total, bijective mapping is lossless (D7). 'Any species' has no defined meaning yet, so the report should not have prescribed UNKNOWN (D5).

errata.title: No source is pinned
errata.detail: Every source has a title, DOI or permanent URL and version, but none has a SHA-256 of the reviewed bytes. Pinning is a Phase 1 task.

errata.title: The change request now lives in the repository
errata.detail: It is at docs/scientific-remediation/pre-review-2026-09-15/ with the tools that produce it.

errata.title: The change request answered questions the packets do not ask
errata.detail: Corrected: it now carries 5,829 answers, exactly the set the 650 packets ask.

errata.title: S12 overstated the data-use ordering defect
errata.detail: security.data_use is already a set-like path in the normalization rules, and normalised contracts compare as EXACT whatever the element order. The narrower real defect: compare_contracts does not normalise internally, so a caller skipping that stage gets INCOMPATIBLE from ordering alone, and equal on a set of DUO codes carries no subsumption.

errata.title: The findings that survived replay are now executable
errata.detail: Fifteen defects and eight guards live in scientific-checks/v0.1/cases.json and run in both implementations. Prefer those tests over this report's prose where the two disagree.

systemic_findings.title: semantic.concept is a version-bound self-reference, so it carries no scientific meaning and breaks across versions
systemic_findings.field: semantic.concept (fixed value and the equal comparison rule); source: scripts/build_standard.py profile_concept()
systemic_findings.current: Fixed const '<profile ref>/v0.1#concept', i.e. https://biosimulant.com/.../profiles/<domain>/<name>/v0.1#concept, compared with operator 'equal'. The term has no definition, no label, no axioms and no mapping to any external vocabulary. It is also minted inside the versioned profile document IRI.
systemic_findings.proposed: Two changes. (a) Keep a Biosimulant-controlled term but mint it in a version-independent namespace, e.g. https://biosimulant.com/standards/model-compatibility/terms/<domain>/<name> , with a label, a textual definition, and its own term-level version; the profile document stays versioned. (b) Because the concept only restates profile identity, add semantic.ontology_terms as a required item for every non-core domain profile: at least one CURIE from a Bioregistry-registered prefix (OBI, UBERON, CL, CHEBI, PATO, NCIT, EFO, GO, SO, MONDO as appropriate), each with ontology, uri, version and relation (exact-match | broad-match | narrow-match), compared with term-equivalent / term-subsumes against a pinned ontology snapshot, missing snapshot -> UNKNOWN.
systemic_findings.reason: As built, the rule is tautological: validation already forces both contracts to hold the same const, so the equal rule can never fail between two valid contracts of the same profile - it duplicates profile_refs and checks nothing about science. Worse, because the IRI embeds /v0.1, a v0.2 profile mints a different concept IRI, so every v0.1 port becomes INCOMPATIBLE with a v0.2 port even when the scientific meaning is unchanged. Identifier stability across versions is exactly what OBO FP-003 and the W3C hash-URI guidance are for. A compatibility contract that claims to encode scientific meaning must anchor that meaning in a maintained vocabulary, otherwise two independently built ports can never agree except by adopting the same Biosimulant profile.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add a cross-version fixture: v0.1 concept vs v0.2 concept of the same term must not be INCOMPATIBLE. Add comparison-unknown-semantic-ontology-terms (no pinned snapshot -> UNKNOWN) and comparison-direct-ontology-term-subsumes (child term -> parent term). Every positive fixture gains a real ontology_terms entry.

systemic_findings.title: semantic.subject is uncontrolled free text compared by string equality
systemic_findings.field: semantic.subject (required item, schema {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 4096}, operator 'equal')
systemic_findings.current: Any string up to 4096 characters. Generated positive fixtures use one placeholder per domain: 'biological_sample', 'nervous_system', 'data_value', 'exposed_biological_system', and so on. Comparison is exact string equality.
systemic_findings.proposed: Replace the free string with a CURIE from a registered prefix (UBERON, CL, OBI, ENVO, NCBITaxon, CHEBI as fits the domain), pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*:[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ with the prefix resolvable in a pinned Bioregistry snapshot. Compare with term-subsumes (the target's subject must subsume the source's subject) against a pinned ontology snapshot; no snapshot -> UNKNOWN. Demote to conditional-required: required only where the sampled entity changes the meaning of the value (tissue, cell type, biofluid, environment), not for profiles whose value is entity-independent.
systemic_findings.reason: String equality on uncontrolled text produces both error directions. False INCOMPATIBLE: 'blood_plasma' vs 'plasma' vs 'UBERON:0001969' describe the same specimen and compare unequal (verified against the engine: metabolite-concentration with subject 'biological_sample' vs 'blood_plasma' returns INCOMPATIBLE). False DIRECT_COMPATIBLE: the domain placeholder 'biological_sample' matches itself across plasma, CSF, tumour biopsy and faecal samples, which are not interchangeable for any concentration or abundance measurement. Anatomical and specimen semantics are exactly what UBERON, CL and OBI maintain, including the subsumption hierarchy that makes 'is this sample type acceptable' answerable.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Replace every positive fixture placeholder with a real CURIE. Add comparison-direct-semantic-subject-subsumes (UBERON:0001969 blood plasma -> UBERON:0000178 blood must not be INCOMPATIBLE when the target is the broader term) and comparison-unknown-semantic-subject-no-snapshot.

systemic_findings.title: Direct compatibility hides required transformations: optional fields present on both contracts are never compared
systemic_findings.field: Comparison rule generation (scripts/build_standard.py, rules derived only from required_items) and python/src/.../compare.py _rules()
systemic_findings.current: When profile refs are supplied, the engine evaluates only the rules the profile declares, which are generated only from required_items. spec/v0.1/catalogue/items.json states the opposite for all 266 items: 'Checked only when the profile requires it or both contracts include it.'
systemic_findings.proposed: Generate comparison rules with missing:'ignore' for every declared-on-both-sides item that can change interpretation, at minimum: measurement.unit (unit-convertible), measurement.scale, measurement.normalization, measurement.baseline, measurement.aggregation, identifiers.namespace and identifiers.namespace_version, representation.ordering, representation.feature_space, dimensions.axes, lifecycle.time_unit, origin.type. missing:'ignore' gives exactly the documented semantics: skip when either side is silent, compare when both declare.
systemic_findings.reason: Verified against the engine on transcriptome/single-cell-expression-matrix: source declaring measurement {quantity: read_count, scale: count} and target declaring {quantity: log1p_normalized_expression, scale: log} returns DIRECT_COMPATIBLE with no finding. Raw counts and log-normalised expression are not interchangeable inputs to any model; feeding one where the other is expected is a silent scientific error, and library-size normalisation plus a log transform is precisely a declared, lossy, non-invertible transformation. The same check returns DIRECT_COMPATIBLE for identifiers.namespace 'ensembl.gene' vs 'hgnc.symbol', which is a many-to-many mapping with real loss. This directly violates the standard's own promise that direct compatibility never hides a required transformation, and it contradicts the published item semantics.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Every profile that permits a numeric value needs comparison-lossy-normalization (counts vs log-normalised -> LOSSY_CONVERSION_REQUIRES_APPROVAL or INCOMPATIBLE) and comparison-mapping-required (ensembl.gene vs hgnc.symbol -> mapping required, not DIRECT).
systemic_findings.applies: all 650; demonstrated on the 526 profiles that do not require measurement.unit and the 552 that do not require identifiers.namespace

systemic_findings.title: unit-convertible is a four-row lookup table, not dimensional analysis, and no rule ties a unit to its quantity
systemic_findings.field: spec/v0.1/rules/unit-conversions.json and the unit-convertible operator in both implementations
systemic_findings.current: The whole conversion table is nM->uM, uM->nM, mM->uM, uM->mM. measurement.unit is validated only as {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 128}. Verified engine results: g vs kg -> INCOMPATIBLE; Cel vs K -> INCOMPATIBLE; 1/s vs /min -> INCOMPATIBLE; uM vs mol/L -> INCOMPATIBLE; a firing rate declared in kg validates with no finding.
systemic_findings.proposed: Adopt UCUM 2.2 as the unit grammar: validate measurement.unit as a parseable UCUM expression, and implement unit-convertible as UCUM dimensional analysis (equal dimension vectors -> convertible; factor from the canonical form). Handle affine units explicitly (Cel/[degF] convert to K with an offset, so only whole quantities convert, never differences or ratios). Constrain each profile's unit to the dimension of its quantity (e.g. amount-of-substance concentration N.L^-3 for concentration profiles) and reject dimensionally impossible units. Mass-concentration to molar-concentration (mg/L vs uM) requires an external molar mass and must resolve to a declared parameterised transformation, not DIRECT and not INCOMPATIBLE.
systemic_findings.reason: Every one of those verified results is scientifically wrong. g and kg are the same quantity with a factor of 1000; /min and 1/s are the same quantity; uM and mol/L are the same quantity; Cel and K differ by an additive offset. Returning INCOMPATIBLE for convertible units makes the standard block valid couplings, and accepting kg for a firing rate makes it approve impossible ones. UCUM exists to answer exactly this question and is the unit code system used by HL7/FHIR and LOINC.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add per-dimension conversion fixtures: g<->kg and s<->min and 1/s<->/min lossless; Cel<->K lossless for absolute values but flagged for differences; uM<->mol/L lossless; mg/L vs uM requires a declared molar-mass parameter; kg vs Hz INCOMPATIBLE. Remove the blanket nM->uM fixture from profiles whose quantity is not a molar concentration.
systemic_findings.applies: all 650; the 124 profiles that require measurement.unit are directly affected

systemic_findings.title: biological_context.species is a single taxon compared by string equality, with no subsumption and an unsafe wildcard direction
systemic_findings.current: Schema: 'any' or ^NCBITaxon:[1-9][0-9]*$, one value. The operator is implemented as source == target or target in (None, 'any', 'unspecified'). Verified: source 'any' vs target NCBITaxon:9606 -> INCOMPATIBLE; source NCBITaxon:9606 vs target 'any' -> DIRECT_COMPATIBLE. Every generated positive fixture uses NCBITaxon:9606, including ecology, evolution, microbiology and virology profiles.
systemic_findings.proposed: (a) Compare with term-subsumes over a pinned NCBI Taxonomy snapshot so that a strain or subspecies satisfies a port that asks for the species (NCBITaxon:511145 E. coli K-12 MG1655 satisfies NCBITaxon:562 E. coli), and so a broader source does not silently satisfy a narrower target. (b) A source of 'any' against a specific target must return UNKNOWN, not INCOMPATIBLE - it is absent evidence, not a contradiction. (c) Replace the single value with a role-typed set for profiles where more than one organism is in scope: biological_context.taxa[] with {taxon, role: host | pathogen | community_member | donor}, required for virology, microbiology, epidemiology and host-pathogen profiles. (d) For community-level profiles (ecology/species-abundance, microbiology/taxonomic-abundance, microbiology/community-composition and similar), a single species is the wrong cardinality: require the taxonomy namespace and release plus a feature universe, and make species conditional.
systemic_findings.reason: Absent evidence and contradiction are different states, and the current asymmetry gets both backwards in the unsafe direction: a port that declares nothing about species is allowed to feed a port that requires human. Equality without the taxonomic hierarchy blocks correct couplings between strain-level and species-level declarations, which is the normal case in microbiology. And a human taxon on an ecology abundance vector or a viral titre is not a valid scientific example: for virology and microbiology the host and the organism measured are different entities, so one species field cannot express either.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Rebuild positive fixtures per domain with a plausible taxon (virology: pathogen NCBITaxon:2697049 with host NCBITaxon:9606; ecology: a real community with a taxonomy release). Add comparison-unknown-species-any-source, comparison-direct-species-strain-satisfies-species, and keep comparison-incompatible-species for a genuine cross-species contradiction.
systemic_findings.applies: 575 profiles requiring species; the 75 without it (core, chemical, simulation) are unaffected

systemic_findings.title: Unit, scale and axis values in the generated fixtures are chosen by substring matching on the profile name
systemic_findings.field: scripts/build_standard.py measurement_unit(), example_value() scale branch, axis_names()
systemic_findings.current: Unit and scale are selected by testing whether the profile name contains a token. 'concentration' contains the substring 'ratio', so all 14 concentration profiles get scale 'probability'. 'integrated-embedding' contains 'rate', so it gets unit 1/s. 'proliferation-rate', 'migration-rate' and 'glomerular-filtration-rate' contain 'ratio' and get scale 'probability'. Axis names come from the same mechanism: any name containing 'volume' gets image axes [x, y], so stroke-volume and volume-of-distribution get spatial axes, while ct-volume and mri-volume - which are three-dimensional - get only two.
systemic_findings.proposed: Delete the substring heuristics. Declare quantity kind, unit dimension, measurement scale and axis structure explicitly per profile in source/catalogue.review.json, reviewed one profile at a time. Separate Stevens' measurement level (nominal | ordinal | interval | ratio) from the value domain and transform: add measurement.transform (identity | log2 | log10 | ln | logit) and use 'proportion' for bounded [0,1] fractions, reserving 'probability' for values that are probabilities of an event. The log base must be explicit, because log2 and log10 fold changes are different numbers.
systemic_findings.reason: A generated example that is scientifically wrong is worse than no example, because downstream implementers copy it: the positive fixture is the profile's worked example of a valid contract. A micromolar concentration is a ratio-scale quantity with a true zero, not a probability; a fraction bounded in [0,1] is a proportion, which is not the same claim as a probability; and Celsius is an interval scale, so 'ratio' is wrong for body temperature even though the unit is right. Stevens' levels also determine which operations are meaningful, so the scale value is not cosmetic - it decides whether averaging or ratio comparison is defensible.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Every positive fixture for the 124 measurement profiles must be regenerated from reviewed per-profile values; see the per-profile unit and scale corrections.
systemic_findings.applies: 124 profiles requiring measurement.unit; 89 profiles requiring dimensions.axes

systemic_findings.title: The single transformation fixture asserts a molar-concentration conversion for every measurement profile
systemic_findings.field: scripts/build_standard.py fixture generation; fixture comparison-lossless-unit-conversion in 124 profiles
systemic_findings.current: All 124 profiles that require measurement.unit receive the same fixture: source unit nM, target unit uM, expected LOSSLESS_CONVERSION_AVAILABLE - including firing-rate, body-temperature, heart-rate, simulation-time, retention-time, body-mass and polygenic-score. Verified: neuroscience/firing-rate with nM vs uM returns LOSSLESS_CONVERSION_AVAILABLE.
systemic_findings.proposed: Generate the conversion fixture from the profile's own declared unit dimension (mass: g<->kg; time: s<->min; frequency: 1/s<->/min; molar concentration: nM<->uM; temperature: Cel<->K flagged as affine), and add a dimensional-mismatch fixture (the profile's unit vs a unit of another dimension -> INCOMPATIBLE).
systemic_findings.reason: The fixture certifies, as a passing conformance test in both implementations, that a neuronal firing rate can be converted from nanomolar to micromolar. It is dimensionally impossible. Because the fixtures are the cross-language conformance suite, this false claim is what the Python and TypeScript packages are being tested to agree on.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Replace comparison-lossless-unit-conversion in all 124 profiles; add comparison-incompatible-unit-dimension.

systemic_findings.title: The unit contradiction fixture asserts that g and kg are incompatible
systemic_findings.current: The contradiction unit is hard-coded as 'kg' (or 's' when the profile's unit is already kg). For the six profiles whose unit is g - physiology/body-mass, ecology/biomass, microbiology/biofilm-biomass, chemical/exact-mass, metabolome/mass-spectral-peak, metabolome/mass-spectrum - the fixture therefore asserts that kg vs g must be INCOMPATIBLE. Verified: the engine returns INCOMPATIBLE.
systemic_findings.proposed: Choose the contradiction unit as one of a different dimension from the profile's own unit (for a mass quantity use s or Hz, never another mass unit), and add the matching g<->kg lossless conversion fixture.
systemic_findings.reason: Kilograms and grams are the same quantity; a contract expressed in one converts exactly to the other. Certifying that pairing as a contradiction means the standard blocks a correct coupling and, being a fixture, freezes the error into the conformance suite.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Fix comparison-incompatible-measurement-unit for the 6 mass profiles; add comparison-lossless g<->kg.
systemic_findings.applies: 6 profiles with unit g; the pattern is wrong for any profile whose unit shares a dimension with kg

systemic_findings.title: No profile has a lossy or inference fixture, although the transformation policy declares both paths
systemic_findings.field: transformation_policy {lossless: allow, lossy: approval, inference: approval}; fixture_groups.transformations
systemic_findings.current: 526 profiles have an empty transformations group and the remaining 124 have exactly one lossless fixture. No profile anywhere exercises LOSSY_CONVERSION_REQUIRES_APPROVAL or the inference path, so the approval branches of the policy are untested in both implementations.
systemic_findings.proposed: Require, for every profile whose transformation_policy admits them, at least one lossy fixture (e.g. continuous value binned to an ordinal category; log-normalised from counts) and one inference fixture (a value that can only be produced by a model, e.g. imputed or deconvolved), each with the expected approval status.
systemic_findings.reason: The review instruction that lossy conversions and inference must be clearly identified cannot be verified for any profile in the release. An untested approval path is where silent scientific substitution happens, because the failure mode is a status that quietly reads as compatible.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add lossy and inference fixtures to all 650 profiles.

systemic_findings.title: UNKNOWN is only tested for a missing source; a missing target is never exercised
systemic_findings.current: Each unknown fixture removes the field from the source contract only. The engine treats either side missing as UNKNOWN, but no fixture pins that behaviour for the target side.
systemic_findings.proposed: Add the mirrored fixture (field absent from the target) for each required field.
systemic_findings.reason: Missing evidence must return UNKNOWN regardless of which port is silent; a one-sided test lets an asymmetric regression through. The behaviour is currently correct in both implementations, so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add comparison-unknown-target-<field> for every required field.

systemic_findings.title: representation.kind uses exact equality, so lossless re-encodings are reported as contradictions
systemic_findings.current: Verified: dense_vector vs sparse_vector on transcriptome/single-cell-expression-matrix returns INCOMPATIBLE. Allowed kind sets are derived from the coarse applies_to families, so core/scalar-quantity permits matrix, tensor and table.
systemic_findings.proposed: Declare lossless representation transformations (dense_vector <-> sparse_vector, matrix <-> table with a declared schema) and return LOSSLESS_CONVERSION_AVAILABLE; narrow each profile's allowed kinds to those its scientific meaning admits (core/scalar-quantity should allow scalar only).
systemic_findings.reason: Sparse and dense encodings of the same vector carry identical information, so INCOMPATIBLE is a false negative. It is the safe direction of error, which is why this is not blocking on its own - but for scalar-quantity the allowed set contradicts the profile's own name and intended use.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add comparison-lossless-representation-kind; fix the allowed-kind enum for core/scalar-quantity and the other scalar profiles.
systemic_findings.applies: all 650; the allowed-set contradiction affects the 395 profiles carrying the full 8-kind set

systemic_findings.title: Identifier, consent and data-use fixtures carry placeholder values, and no namespace is constrained to a real registry
systemic_findings.field: identifiers.namespace, identifiers.namespace_version (98 profiles); security.data_use, security.consent_scope (50 clinical profiles)
systemic_findings.current: Positive fixtures use 'example-namespace', 'example-namespace-version', 'example-consent-scope' and ['example-data_use']. The schemas accept any string; data_use is compared with 'equal' on an array, so element order changes the result.
systemic_findings.proposed: Constrain identifiers.namespace to a Bioregistry-registered prefix resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, and namespace_version to the namespace's own release identifier (e.g. ensembl.gene with release 114). Replace security.data_use with DUO CURIEs (DUO:0000042 general research use and similar), normalise as a set, and compare by DUO subsumption: the target's permitted uses must subsume the source's declared use. Give consent_scope the same treatment.
systemic_findings.reason: A positive fixture is the normative worked example; a placeholder namespace teaches implementers that any string is acceptable, which defeats the purpose of requiring a versioned identifier namespace. For the clinical profiles the consequence is governance, not just tidiness: order-sensitive equality on a data-use array can wrongly block a lawful data flow or, when the arrays happen to match, pass one that consent does not cover. DUO exists as the GA4GH standard for exactly this comparison.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Replace all placeholder identifier and security values with real registered values; add set-order and DUO-subsumption comparison fixtures.
systemic_findings.applies: 98 profiles with identifiers; 50 clinical profiles with security fields

systemic_findings.title: Uncertainty, detection limits and censoring are never required, though they change whether values are comparable
systemic_findings.field: uncertainty.* and measurement.detection_limits, currently candidate-recommended only
systemic_findings.current: No profile requires any uncertainty item. missingness appears as a candidate in 475 packets, censoring in 400, detection_limits in 450.
systemic_findings.proposed: Make them conditional-required where the science demands it: uncertainty.censoring for phenotype/time-to-event and clinical/survival-outcome; measurement.detection_limits for every concentration, titre and MIC profile; uncertainty.missingness for every matrix profile, distinguishing a structural zero from an unobserved value.
systemic_findings.reason: A survival time without its censoring indicator is not interpretable and will be silently treated as an observed event. A concentration below the lower limit of quantification is not a measurement of zero, which is why bioanalytical guidance requires the limits to travel with the data. In single-cell matrices, zeros are mostly genuine low counts rather than missing values, so a port that treats them as missing and one that treats them as zero are not interchangeable.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add missing-evidence fixtures (censoring absent -> UNKNOWN) for the affected profiles.
systemic_findings.applies: conditional across the 124 measurement profiles, matrix profiles and survival profiles

systemic_findings.title: Time-series and event profiles do not require a time unit, time origin or sampling rule
systemic_findings.field: lifecycle.time_unit, lifecycle.time_origin, lifecycle.sampling, lifecycle.interpolation (candidates in 350 packets); dimensions.axes ['time'] in 25 profiles
systemic_findings.current: A profile can require a time axis while leaving the time unit, the origin of the clock and the sampling regime undeclared. core/regular-time-series and core/irregular-time-series differ in exactly this respect yet impose the same requirements.
systemic_findings.proposed: For every profile whose axes include time, require lifecycle.time_unit (UCUM), lifecycle.time_origin, and lifecycle.sampling; require lifecycle.interpolation for irregular series; and record the domain's own conventions where they exist (BIDS/NWB for electrophysiology).
systemic_findings.reason: Two time series that agree on every declared field can still be a 1 kHz recording and a daily series. Sampling rate and epoch are part of what makes time-indexed values comparable, and the electrophysiology community already standardises them.
systemic_findings.fixtures: Add comparison-unknown-lifecycle-time-unit and a sampling-mismatch fixture for the time-axis profiles.
systemic_findings.applies: 25 profiles with a time axis; 76 event/state profiles

artifact.compression.rationale: Required where the consumer must decompress.

artifact.encryption.rationale: Required where the artifact is encrypted at rest.

artifact.format.rationale: For artifact and file ports the format is the contract; should be an EDAM format term or a media type.

artifact.format_version.rationale: Format versions change what can be read.

artifact.schema_ref.rationale: A tabular or structured artifact needs its schema.

artifact.sha256.rationale: Pins the artifact bytes; the standard already requires digests for published references.

biological_context.age.rationale: Context that supports interpretation without gating compatibility.

biological_context.assay.rationale: Required where the assay defines the quantity (titres, scores, intensities).

biological_context.cell_line.rationale: Required for cell-line experiments; should be a Cellosaurus identifier.

biological_context.compartment.rationale: Required where the same analyte differs by compartment (plasma versus tissue, intra- versus extracellular).

biological_context.culture_system.rationale: 2D, 3D and organoid systems are not interchangeable.

biological_context.denominator.rationale: For any rate or proportion, the denominator is part of the quantity.

biological_context.disease.rationale: Required where disease state changes the value's meaning.

biological_context.geography.rationale: Required for spatially indexed epidemiological data.

biological_context.intervention.rationale: Required for perturbation data, with agent, dose, duration and route.

biological_context.intervention.schedule.rationale: Part of the perturbation identity for repeat dosing.

biological_context.oxygen.rationale: Oxygen tension changes metabolic and hypoxia-related values.

biological_context.sampling_frame.rationale: Required for surveillance and survey data.

biological_context.sex.rationale: As above; may become conditional for sex-specific references.

biological_context.strain.rationale: Required for microbial, viral and inbred-animal work.

biological_context.substrate.rationale: Required for adhesion, migration and biofilm assays.

biological_context.tissue.rationale: Required where the value is tissue-dependent.

constraints[].id.rationale: Required when the profile declares cross-field constraints.

constraints[].operator.rationale: Must come from the published operator vocabulary.

constraints[].profile_ref.rationale: The profile the constraint belongs to.

dimensions.axes[].coordinates_ref.rationale: Required for physical or genomic coordinate axes.

dimensions.axes[].dynamic.rationale: Declares whether the size is fixed at bind time.

dimensions.axes[].labels_ref.rationale: Required where the axis is labelled by entities rather than positions.

dimensions.axes[].labels_sha256.rationale: Pins the label set so two ports can prove they share a feature universe.

dimensions.axes[].meaning.rationale: What the axis indexes is the scientific content of the shape.

dimensions.axes[].name.rationale: An axis without a name cannot be aligned.

dimensions.axes[].ordering.rationale: Order determines whether position i is comparable across ports.

dimensions.axes[].size.rationale: Required where a fixed size is part of the contract.

dimensions.axes[].unit.rationale: Required for physical axes (time, length, concentration, m/z).

dimensions.dose_axis.rationale: For dose- and concentration-response profiles, the dose axis and its unit.

dimensions.feature_labels_ref.rationale: The feature universe must be resolvable, not implied by position.

dimensions.feature_labels_sha256.rationale: Pins the feature universe by digest.

dimensions.orientation.rationale: Patient or specimen orientation prevents left-right and anterior-posterior errors.

dimensions.origin.rationale: The coordinate origin anchors the grid in space.

dimensions.pixel_spacing.rationale: Without spacing, voxel indices carry no physical scale.

dimensions.slice_thickness.rationale: Part of the physical geometry of a volume.

dimensions.spatial_axes.rationale: For imaging and spatial data, which axes are spatial and in what order.

dimensions.time_axis.rationale: Identifies the time axis where one exists.

identifiers.ambiguity_handling.rationale: Required where one-to-many mappings are possible.

identifiers.canonicalization.rationale: Required where an identifier has several textual forms.

identifiers.case_policy.rationale: Case handling is a frequent source of silent mismatches.

identifiers.coding_system.rationale: For clinical codes, the code system is the meaning (ICD-10 versus SNOMED CT).

identifiers.coding_version.rationale: Clinical code semantics change between versions.

identifiers.deprecated_handling.rationale: Required where retired identifiers may appear.

identifiers.edge_namespace.rationale: Where edges carry their own identifiers.

identifiers.entity_type.rationale: Gene, transcript, protein and variant identifiers are not interchangeable.

identifiers.mapping_refs.rationale: Required whenever the two ports use different namespaces (S3).

identifiers.mapping_refs[].cardinality.rationale: One-to-many mappings are lossy and must be declared as such.

identifiers.mapping_refs[].coverage.rationale: Partial coverage makes a mapping lossy.

identifiers.mapping_refs[].ref.rationale: The mapping resource must be resolvable.

identifiers.node_namespace.rationale: For graphs, what the node identifiers are.

identifiers.structure_hash.rationale: Pins a chemical or macromolecular structure.

identifiers.taxonomy_namespace.rationale: For community profiles, the taxonomy and its release define the labels.

identifiers.taxonomy_version.rationale: Taxonomies are renamed and re-parented between releases.

identifiers.transcript_reference.rationale: HGVS-style notation is meaningless without the transcript and version.

identifiers.unmapped_handling.rationale: What happens to unmapped features decides whether a mapping is lossy.

identifiers.variant_notation.rationale: The notation system (HGVS, SPDI, VCF) defines how to read the variant.

lifecycle.causality.rationale: Whether the value may depend on future samples (filtering versus smoothing).

lifecycle.evolutionary_time.rationale: Required for phylogenetic time axes, with the calibration.

lifecycle.interpolation.rationale: Required for irregular series consumed as continuous signals.

lifecycle.observation_period.rationale: Required for incidence and surveillance measures.

lifecycle.sampling.rationale: Regular versus irregular sampling and the interval.

lifecycle.temporal_meaning.rationale: Whether the value is instantaneous, an interval average or cumulative.

lifecycle.time_origin.rationale: The epoch that t=0 refers to.

lifecycle.window.rationale: Required where the value is computed over a window (firing rates, moving averages).

measurement.aggregation.rationale: Required where the value summarises repeats or a population (mean, median, per-cell versus per-sample).

measurement.baseline.rationale: Required for fold changes, deltas and response values, which are undefined without their reference.

measurement.batch_correction.rationale: Required for matrices: batch-corrected values cannot be pooled with uncorrected ones.

measurement.calibration_ref.rationale: Required where results are only comparable after calibration to a standard (immunoassays, PET SUV, WHO units).

measurement.control.rationale: Required for assay readouts expressed relative to a control.

measurement.detection_limits.rationale: Required for concentrations, titres and MIC values, where values below the limit are not zeros.

measurement.evolutionary_distance.rationale: Required where the distance's substitution model must travel with the value.

measurement.normalization.rationale: Required for every abundance, intensity or expression value: raw and normalised values are not interchangeable (S3).

measurement.quantity.rationale: The quantity kind; must resolve to an external quantity term rather than a self-reference (S1).

measurement.rate_basis.rationale: For every rate profile: per-capita, per person-time, per contact and per cell are different quantities.

measurement.reference_range.rationale: Clinically useful; not a compatibility gate.

measurement.response_direction.rationale: Required for response curves, where the sign convention changes interpretation.

measurement.scale.rationale: Stevens level, separated from transform and value domain (S6).

origin.edge_evidence.rationale: Required for interaction graphs: predicted and experimental edges differ.

origin.method.rationale: Required where the method defines the quantity.

origin.method_version.rationale: Required where method versions change values.

origin.model_digest.rationale: Required where a model produced the value.

origin.observed_at.rationale: Required where the observation time matters.

origin.processing_pipeline_ref.rationale: Required for imaging and omics pipelines.

origin.protocol_ref.rationale: Required where a protocol defines the assay.

origin.registration_ref.rationale: Required where spatial registration underlies the value.

origin.segmentation_method.rationale: Required where segmentation produces the value.

origin.software_version.rationale: Required for computed values whose results change between versions.

origin.source_sha256.rationale: Pins the source bytes for derived data.

origin.transformation_chain.rationale: The applied transformations are what distinguish raw from processed values (S3).

representation.canonicalization.rationale: Required where the same value has several textual forms (sequences, SMILES, variants).

representation.channel_order.rationale: For multichannel images, channel order defines what each plane is.

representation.circularity.rationale: Required for circular genomes and plasmids.

representation.coordinate_system.rationale: For any positional data: assembly, origin and 0- versus 1-based conventions silently corrupt coordinates.

representation.directed.rationale: Directedness changes the claim a graph makes.

representation.edge_schema.rationale: For graphs, the edge schema defines what an edge asserts.

representation.encoding.rationale: Required for sequence and artifact ports.

representation.endianness.rationale: Byte order is an artifact-level concern handled by the format.

representation.feature_space.rationale: Required for every vector or matrix: the feature universe and its version define what position i means.

representation.interval_convention.rationale: Half-open versus closed intervals is the classic off-by-one in genomic ranges.

representation.isotope_state.rationale: Required for tracer and exact-mass work.

representation.layout.rationale: Required for matrices and tensors where row-major versus column-major changes interpretation of a flat buffer.

representation.left_normalized.rationale: Variant normalisation determines whether two records are the same variant.

representation.masking.rationale: Soft- versus hard-masking affects downstream use.

representation.multigraph.rationale: Required where parallel edges are meaningful.

representation.node_schema.rationale: For graphs, the node schema defines what a node is.

representation.ordering.rationale: Required whenever the value is an ordered array; an unordered feature vector cannot be aligned.

representation.precision.rationale: Precision loss matters for checkpoint and artifact exchange but rarely gates scientific compatibility.

representation.protonation_state.rationale: Required for docking and physics-based modelling.

representation.quality_encoding.rationale: Required for read data, where the quality offset differs by platform.

representation.reference_assembly.rationale: Coordinates are meaningless without the assembly and its patch level.

representation.sparsity.rationale: Required for sparse encodings, together with whether an absent entry is a zero or an unobserved value.

representation.state_order.rationale: Required where categorical states have a defined order.

representation.stereochemistry.rationale: For chemical structures, stereochemistry changes the molecule and its activity.

representation.strand.rationale: Strand changes the biological claim for stranded data.

representation.tautomer_state.rationale: Required for docking and property prediction.

representation.weight_semantics.rationale: An edge weight may be a probability, a correlation, a count or a distance; these are not interchangeable.

security.deidentification.rationale: For human-subject data, the de-identification level is a governance precondition, not a preference.

security.export_control.rationale: Required for controlled biological or clinical data.

security.license.rationale: Required where redistribution terms restrict use.

security.residency.rationale: Required where data may not leave a jurisdiction.

security.workspace_boundary.rationale: The boundary that a compatibility decision must not cross silently.

semantic.ancestral_state.rationale: Required for phylogenetic reconstructions, where the state's polarity is part of the claim.

semantic.cell_state.rationale: Useful context; not a compatibility gate on its own.

semantic.consequence.rationale: Required where the consequence term is the value's meaning.

semantic.endpoint.rationale: Required where the value is an assay or clinical endpoint whose definition changes the number (response, survival, toxicity); optional elsewhere.

semantic.entity.rationale: Required where a specific molecular or cellular entity identifies the value.

semantic.intended_use.rationale: Declared intended use supports the governance boundary but must not act as a compatibility gate.

semantic.model_formalism.rationale: Required for simulation ports, where the formalism determines what the state means.

semantic.ontology_snapshot_ref.rationale: Required whenever ontology_terms are compared, since term-equivalent and term-subsumes need a pinned snapshot.

semantic.ontology_snapshot_sha256.rationale: As above: the snapshot must be pinned by digest for a reproducible comparison.

semantic.ontology_terms.rationale: Carries the external scientific meaning that semantic.concept does not (S1); at least one CURIE from a registered prefix with ontology, version and relation.

semantic.ontology_terms[].label.rationale: A human-readable label aids review but must never be the compared value.

semantic.ontology_terms[].ontology.rationale: The source ontology determines which snapshot is used for subsumption.

semantic.ontology_terms[].relation.rationale: Exact, broad and narrow matches support different compatibility conclusions.

semantic.ontology_terms[].uri.rationale: The term IRI or CURIE is the compared value; without it the mapping cannot be resolved.

semantic.ontology_terms[].version.rationale: Ontology releases obsolete and re-parent terms, so the release must be pinned.

semantic.process.rationale: Required where the biological process defines the quantity (rates, fluxes, transitions).

semantic.qualifiers.rationale: Free qualifiers cannot be compared safely until they are term-bound; keep optional and non-comparing.

semantic.role.rationale: Distinguishes the port's role (input, output, covariate) without changing the scientific identity of the value.

semantic.variant_class.rationale: Required where variant class changes interpretation.

uncertainty.confidence_level.rationale: An interval without its level is uninterpretable.

uncertainty.imputation.rationale: Imputed values must not silently substitute for observed ones.

uncertainty.interval.rationale: Required where an interval is provided.

uncertainty.kind.rationale: Required wherever an uncertainty value is present, to say what it is.

uncertainty.missingness.rationale: For matrices and vectors: whether an absent entry is a zero, a non-detect or unobserved (S13).

uncertainty.variance.rationale: Required where variance travels with the value.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: This profile's value is a single scalar, event or record with no indexed axes, so axis, coordinate and feature-order fields cannot change compatibility.

identifiers.rationale: The value is not indexed by an external entity identifier, so namespace and release cannot change compatibility.

measurement.rationale: The value is categorical, structural or an identity assertion with no measured magnitude, so unit and scale do not apply.

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: This profile carries time-indexed or event data: time unit, origin, sampling and temporal meaning must be required (S14).

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Arrhy: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../cardiopulmonary-renal/arrhythmia-event/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is event, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Arrhythmia Event values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Are event/state meaning, observation tim: No. lifecycle.temporal_meaning, time_unit, time_origin and sampling are candidates rather than requirements, so an instantaneous value, an interval average and a cumulative total are all exchangeable under this profile (S14).

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Arrhythmia Event ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Intracellular pH values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Clinical Endpoint values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Clinical Endpoint ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

profiles.label: Clinical Observation

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Consent scope and data use are required and must be DUO-bound with subsumption comparison (S12).

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference; security uses 'example-consent-scope'.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. See S11.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Deide: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../clinical/deidentification-level/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Deidentification Level values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Survival Outcome values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Regul: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../core/regular-time-series/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Regular Time Series values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Yes, conditionally: whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector or matrix, the feature universe (labels reference plus digest) and its ordering must be required, otherwise position i is undefined across ports.

question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Branching Morphogenesis values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, record, table, artifact, file, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Embryo Stage values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Are event/state meaning, observation tim: No. lifecycle.temporal_meaning, time_unit, time_origin and sampling are candidates rather than requirements, so an instantaneous value, an interval average and a cumulative total are all exchangeable under this profile (S14).

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Embryo Stage ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

security.rationale: The value cannot carry human-subject or licensed data in this profile's intended use, so consent and data-use fields do not apply.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Ecosy: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../ecology/ecosystem-flux/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts.
