It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Ecosystem Flux values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Organism Taxon values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Which identifier namespaces, releases, c: Only Bioregistry-registered prefixes resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, each with the namespace's own release identifier. Canonicalization must be declared where an identifier has several textual forms. Cross-namespace mapping must declare the mapping resource, release, digest, cardinality, coverage and the handling of unmapped features; one-to-many or partial mappings are lossy and must require approval rather than resolving as direct.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Speci: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../ecology/species-abundance/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, artifact, file, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Species Abundance values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit 1 (counts) or a declared density unit, proposed scale count. profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Species Abundance ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.

Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is event, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Reproduction Number values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.

question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Nucleosome Positioning values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Nucleosome Positioning ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

profiles.label: Promoter Activity

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.

fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Evolu: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../evolution/evolutionary-distance/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Evolutionary Distance values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit 1 (substitutions per site), proposed scale ratio. Dimensionless is right, but the substitution model that produced the distance must be declared, because distances from different models are not comparable. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.

question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. profile_findings.field: measurement.unit, measurement.scale (profile requirement and positive fixture)
profile_findings.proposed: unit cM/Mb, or 1 per bp per generation; scale ratio
profile_findings.reason: Recombination rate is per physical distance per generation; 1/s is not that quantity.

profile_findings.title: Conversion fixture asserts a molar-concentration conversion for a non-concentration quantity
profile_findings.current: source nM, target uM, expected LOSSLESS_CONVERSION_AVAILABLE
profile_findings.proposed: a conversion within this profile's own dimension, plus a cross-dimension contradiction fixture (proposed unit: cM/Mb, or 1 per bp per generation)
profile_findings.reason: The fixture certifies a nanomolar-to-micromolar conversion for a quantity that has no molar unit, and both implementations are tested to agree on it.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Quantity, unit and scale are required, and must be corrected per the per-profile table.

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: The value cannot carry human-subject or licensed data in this profile's intended use, so consent and data-use fields do not apply.

fixture_review.positive_note: Declared unit, scale, axes or representation are scientifically wrong - see the profile findings.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Unit is compared, but normalisation, baseline and aggregation are not, so differently normalised values still resolve as direct (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: The only conversion fixture asserts nM->uM for this profile (S7).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Recom: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../evolution/recombination-rate/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Recombination Rate values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1/s' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit cM/Mb, or 1 per bp per generation, proposed scale ratio. Recombination rate is per physical distance per generation; 1/s is not that quantity. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Are event/state meaning, observation tim: No. lifecycle.temporal_meaning, time_unit, time_origin and sampling are candidates rather than requirements, so an instantaneous value, an interval average and a cumulative total are all exchangeable under this profile (S14).

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Recombination Rate ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Gene: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../genome/gene-presence-absence/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Gene Presence/Absence values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Which identifier namespaces, releases, c: Only Bioregistry-registered prefixes resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, each with the namespace's own release identifier. Canonicalization must be declared where an identifier has several textual forms. Cross-namespace mapping must declare the mapping resource, release, digest, cardinality, coverage and the handling of unmapped features; one-to-many or partial mappings are lossy and must require approval rather than resolving as direct.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: This profile's value is a single scalar, event or record with no indexed axes, so axis, coordinate and feature-order fields cannot change compatibility.

identifiers.rationale: The identifier namespace and release define what the entity labels mean.

measurement.rationale: The value is categorical, structural or an identity assertion with no measured magnitude, so unit and scale do not apply.

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: This profile admits artifact or file exchange, so format, format version, schema and digest must be required.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference; identifiers use 'example-namespace'.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Varia: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../genome/variant-consequence/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, record, table, artifact, file, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Variant Consequence values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Which identifier namespaces, releases, c: Only Bioregistry-registered prefixes resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, each with the namespace's own release identifier. Canonicalization must be declared where an identifier has several textual forms. Cross-namespace mapping must declare the mapping resource, release, digest, cardinality, coverage and the handling of unmapped features; one-to-many or partial mappings are lossy and must require approval rather than resolving as direct.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Variant Consequence ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify PET V: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../imaging/pet-volume/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, artifact, file, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies PET Volume values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Yes, conditionally: whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector or matrix, the feature universe (labels reference plus digest) and its ordering must be required, otherwise position i is undefined across ports.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit 'mL' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit Bq/mL, or 1 for SUV, proposed scale ratio. PET voxels are activity concentration or a standardised uptake value; SUV additionally requires the body-weight basis and the uptake time. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Are axis names, order, labels, coordinat: No. [x, y] should be [x, y, z] plus frame time for dynamic studies: A PET volume is three-dimensional and often four-dimensional. Axis names are declared but per-axis meaning, unit, label reference, label digest and coordinate reference are only candidates, so two ports can agree on axis names while indexing different feature universes.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing PET Volume ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. profile_findings.title: Unit and scale acceptable but under-specified
profile_findings.field: measurement.unit, measurement.scale (profile requirement and positive fixture)
profile_findings.proposed: unit 1 (reciprocal dilution) or IU/mL, BAU/mL; scale ordinal with transform log2 for dilution titres; ratio for standardised units

profile_findings.current: source nM, target uM, expected LOSSLESS_CONVERSION_AVAILABLE
profile_findings.proposed: a conversion within this profile's own dimension, plus a cross-dimension contradiction fixture (proposed unit: 1 (reciprocal dilution) or IU/mL, BAU/mL)
profile_findings.reason: The fixture certifies a nanomolar-to-micromolar conversion for a quantity that has no molar unit, and both implementations are tested to agree on it.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Unit is compared, but normalisation, baseline and aggregation are not, so differently normalised values still resolve as direct (S3).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Lipid: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../lipidome-glycome/lipid-concentration/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Lipid Concentration values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Energ: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../metabolome/energy-charge/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Energy Charge values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Energy Charge ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Which identifier namespaces, releases, c: Only Bioregistry-registered prefixes resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, each with the namespace's own release identifier. Canonicalization must be declared where an identifier has several textual forms. Cross-namespace mapping must declare the mapping resource, release, digest, cardinality, coverage and the handling of unmapped features; one-to-many or partial mappings are lossy and must require approval rather than resolving as direct.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Intracellular Metabolite ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.

profile_findings.title: Declared scale wrong for this quantity
profile_findings.field: measurement.unit, measurement.scale (profile requirement and positive fixture)
profile_findings.proposed: unit 1; scale proportion

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Quantity, unit and scale are required, and must be corrected per the per-profile table.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Isoto: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../metabolome/isotope-tracer-fraction/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Metab: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../metabolome/metabolite-abundance/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, artifact, file, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Metabolite Abundance values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit 1 (arbitrary intensity) or a declared molar unit, proposed scale ratio with declared normalization. Untargeted metabolomics abundances are arbitrary intensities; targeted values are molar. The profile must distinguish them. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Which identifier namespaces, releases, c: Only Bioregistry-registered prefixes resolved against a pinned registry snapshot, each with the namespace's own release identifier. Canonicalization must be declared where an identifier has several textual forms. Cross-namespace mapping must declare the mapping resource, release, digest, cardinality, coverage and the handling of unmapped features; one-to-many or partial mappings are lossy and must require approval rather than resolving as direct.

question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: The axes define what each position indexes; required for this profile's non-scalar values.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: This profile admits artifact or file exchange, so format, format version, schema and digest must be required.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, artifact, file, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Untargeted Metabolomics Matrix values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Age and sex: recommended context.

question_answers.Are axis names, order, labels, coordinat: No. Axis names are declared but per-axis meaning, unit, label reference, label digest and coordinate reference are only candidates, so two ports can agree on axis names while indexing different feature universes.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Norma: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../multiomics/normalized-feature-matrix/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, artifact, file, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Normalized Feature Matrix values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Yes, conditionally: whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector or matrix, the feature universe (labels reference plus digest) and its ordering must be required, otherwise position i is undefined across ports.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.
question_answers.Are axis names, order, labels, coordinat: No. Axis names are declared but per-axis meaning, unit, label reference, label digest and coordinate reference are only candidates, so two ports can agree on axis names while indexing different feature universes.

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: This profile's value is a single scalar, event or record with no indexed axes, so axis, coordinate and feature-order fields cannot change compatibility.

identifiers.rationale: The identifier namespace and release define what the entity labels mean.

measurement.rationale: The value is categorical, structural or an identity assertion with no measured magnitude, so unit and scale do not apply.

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Subject Identity values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Neuro: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../neuroscience/neurotransmitter-concentration/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Neurotransmitter Concentration values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit 'uM' and scale 'probability' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit uM or nM, proposed scale ratio. Unit acceptable, scale wrong; the compartment (synaptic cleft, extracellular, tissue) must be declared because it changes the quantity by orders of magnitude. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
