semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: This profile carries time-indexed or event data: time unit, origin, sampling and temporal meaning must be required (S14).

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Spike: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../neuroscience/spike-train/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Spike Train values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Spike Train ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Association Rate values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1/s' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit /(mol/L)/s  i.e. M-1.s-1, proposed scale ratio. kon is second-order: per concentration per time. 1/s is the unit of koff, so the two rate constants are currently declared identically. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Are event/state meaning, observation tim: No. lifecycle.temporal_meaning, time_unit, time_origin and sampling are candidates rather than requirements, so an instantaneous value, an interval average and a cumulative total are all exchangeable under this profile (S14).

profile_findings.title: Declared unit wrong for this quantity

profile_findings.proposed: unit mol/L for Kd/Ki, or 1 for pKd/pKi; scale ratio for Kd, interval for pKd

Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Concentration Response Curve values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Yes, conditionally: whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector or matrix, the feature universe (labels reference plus digest) and its ordering must be required, otherwise position i is undefined across ports.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit 'uM' and scale 'probability' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit response unit over a concentration axis in uM, proposed scale ratio. Same axis error as the dose-response curve, plus the probability-scale bug; the concentration axis unit and the response unit are two different declarations. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Are axis names, order, labels, coordinat: No. [time] should be [concentration] with the concentration unit on the axis: The independent variable is concentration, not time. Axis names are declared but per-axis meaning, unit, label reference, label digest and coordinate reference are only candidates, so two ports can agree on axis names while indexing different feature universes.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.

fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).

question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit dose unit plus an interval (e.g. mg every 12 h), proposed scale ratio. A schedule is a dose quantity plus a timing rule; a dimensionless '1' captures neither. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify EC50: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../pharmacology/ec50/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies EC50 values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Plasma Concentration values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Bioma: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../phenotype/biomarker-value/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Biomarker Value values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit analyte-specific (must be declared), proposed scale ratio. Biomarker values are analyte- and assay-specific; a bare '1' lets two different analytes compare as compatible. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Biomarker Value ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.

fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).

fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Drug: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../phenotype/drug-response-auc/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Drug Response AUC values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Drug Response AUC ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Oxygen Saturation values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Oxygen Saturation ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

profiles.label: pH

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Binding Site values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Binding Site ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: Required whenever the port may carry human-subject data: de-identification level and workspace boundary gate the exchange.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Post-: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../proteome/post-translational-modification/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Post-translational Modification values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.

limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.

Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Region Annotation values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Spatial Coordinate values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Spatial Coordinate ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

profiles.label: Spatial Expression Map

structure.rationale: signal_type, dtype and shape in model.yaml carry the transport shape; the contract adds meaning on top and must not restate them.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: The axes define what each position indexes; required for this profile's non-scalar values.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: This profile admits artifact or file exchange, so format, format version, schema and digest must be required.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: The value cannot carry human-subject or licensed data in this profile's intended use, so consent and data-use fields do not apply.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

See S11.

fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Spati: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../spatial/spatial-neighborhood/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Spatial Neighborhood values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify micro: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../transcriptome/microrna-expression/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies microRNA Expression values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Repli: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../virology/replication-rate/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Replication Rate values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Are the quantity, unit, scale, normaliza: No. Current unit '1/s' and scale 'ratio' are wrong or under-specified: proposed unit 1/h, proposed scale ratio. Correct dimension; distinguish the within-host replication rate from the basic reproduction number, which is dimensionless. Normalization, baseline and endpoint are not required at all, and the quantity is a self-referential IRI rather than an external quantity term.
question_answers.Are event/state meaning, observation tim: No. lifecycle.temporal_meaning, time_unit, time_origin and sampling are candidates rather than requirements, so an instantaneous value, an interval average and a cumulative total are all exchangeable under this profile (S14).

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Replication Rate ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.

semantic.rationale: The scientific identity of the value. Included, but the concept must be re-based on an external vocabulary (S1) and subject must be term-bound (S2).

representation.rationale: Which encodings are interchangeable, and when a visible adapter is needed (S11).

dimensions.rationale: Required whenever this profile's value is exchanged as a vector, matrix, tensor or image; not applicable to the scalar case.

identifiers.rationale: Required once the value is indexed by entities (features, genes, taxa, codes) or mapped between namespaces; otherwise inapplicable.

measurement.rationale: Required whenever the port carries a numeric value: unit, scale and normalization must be compared when both sides declare them (S3).

biological_context.rationale: Species is required; it needs subsumption and role typing (S5), plus conditional tissue, cell type, assay and compartment.

lifecycle.rationale: Required where the value is observed at or aggregated over a time window; not a gate for a single static value.

origin.rationale: origin.type and the transformation chain must be required wherever the intended use distinguishes measured from simulated or inferred values; recommended elsewhere.

uncertainty.rationale: Required where the value carries censoring, detection limits or a missingness convention (S13); optional otherwise.

artifact.rationale: The value is exchanged in-memory as a typed contract, not as a file, so format and checksum fields cannot change compatibility.

constraints.rationale: No cross-field relation in this profile changes compatibility beyond the field-level rules already declared.

security.rationale: The value cannot carry human-subject or licensed data in this profile's intended use, so consent and data-use fields do not apply.

fixture_review.positive_note: Schema-valid but not scientifically meaningful: semantic.subject is a domain placeholder token and semantic.concept is a self-reference; species is NCBITaxon:9606 (human) in a domain whose organism of interest is generally not human.
fixture_review.missing_evidence_note: Correct when the source omits a required field; the mirrored case, where the target omits it, has no fixture (S10). A species of 'any' on the source returns INCOMPATIBLE instead of UNKNOWN (S5).
fixture_review.contradiction_note: Declared contradictions return INCOMPATIBLE. The subject contradiction is a string difference, not a scientific contradiction (S2).
fixture_review.direct_note: Optional measurement and identifier fields declared on both ports are never compared, so counts vs log-normalised values and different identifier namespaces resolve as DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3).
fixture_review.conversion_note: No conversion fixture exists; dense<->sparse re-encoding returns INCOMPATIBLE (S11).
fixture_review.lossy_note: No lossy and no inference fixture exists, although transformation_policy declares approval paths for both (S9).

question_answers.Does the proposed concept identify Viral: No. The concept is the self-referential IRI .../virology/viral-phylogeny/v0.1#concept with no definition, label or axioms, and the equal rule on it is tautological for two valid contracts. It is narrow in the sense that nothing else matches it, which is also why it carries no scientific meaning: it restates profile identity. It is also version-bound, so a v0.2 profile would report every v0.1 port as INCOMPATIBLE. See S1.
question_answers.Are the allowed representations complete: The allowed set is scalar, dense_vector, sparse_vector, matrix, tensor, array, record, table, derived from the coarse applies_to family rather than from this profile's meaning. Two allowed representations cannot always connect: dense_vector and sparse_vector are lossless re-encodings but compare INCOMPATIBLE under the equal operator, while record and table require a declared schema mapping. See S11.
question_answers.Which authoritative standards, ontologie: Recorded per decision in this review: UCUM 2.2 and the SI Brochure for units, VIM and ISO 80000-1 for quantity and dimension, Stevens (1946) for measurement level, NCBI Taxonomy for species, UBERON/CL/OBI for specimen and assay semantics, Bioregistry for namespaces, GA4GH DUO for data use, plus the domain sources listed against each profile. No source can be pinned by SHA-256 until the documents are retrieved at sign-off.
question_answers.Which missing value must return UNKNOWN,: UNKNOWN: any required field absent on either side (currently only the source side is fixture-tested, S10); a species of 'any' facing a specific target (currently INCOMPATIBLE, wrong, S5); an ontology or mapping comparison with no pinned snapshot. INCOMPATIBLE: a different concept or subject term with no subsumption path; units of a different dimension; a different measurement scale or normalisation; conflicting compartment or intervention context. Convertible units must never be INCOMPATIBLE, which they currently are for g vs kg, Cel vs K, 1/s vs /min and uM vs mol/L (S4, S8).
question_answers.What uses and scientific claims must thi: That a passing comparison implies Viral Phylogeny values are biologically equivalent, measured under comparable conditions, or fit for clinical or regulatory use. The contract is an interface check only: it cannot detect batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch, or that an upstream model was wrong.
question_answers.Which species, tissue, cell type, diseas: Species: required, but with taxonomic subsumption and, where host and organism differ, role typing (S5). Conditional-required: tissue and cell type where the value is tissue-dependent; assay where the assay defines the quantity; compartment where the same analyte differs by compartment; intervention (agent, dose, duration, route) for perturbation data; cohort and denominator for population measures. Age and sex: recommended context.
question_answers.Does this profile need a versioned ident: Not for the scalar case. It becomes required as soon as the value is indexed by entities or exchanged as an array.
question_answers.Should axes, labels, feature order, coor: Yes for every non-scalar exchange: axes, per-axis meaning and ordering, plus a pinned label set. This profile does not currently require them even though its allowed representations include arrays and matrices.
question_answers.Should quantity, unit, scale, normalizat: Yes. This profile permits numeric values but requires no unit or scale, so two ports differing in unit, normalisation or baseline compare DIRECT_COMPATIBLE (S3). Require quantity, unit (UCUM) and scale whenever a magnitude is carried, and normalization and baseline for any derived or relative value.

profiles.intended_use_assessment: The stated scope - declaring and comparing Viral Phylogeny ports - is coherent, but the packet has no intended-use statement and no limitation list, both of which PROFILE_REVIEW.md requires before the profile can move to reviewed.
limitations_required: A passing comparison does not imply the values were produced under comparable biological or experimental conditions.
The profile does not establish the scientific validity, clinical safety or regulatory suitability of any model using it.
Batch effects, assay bias, population mismatch and upstream model error are outside the contract.
